It exposes a deterministic REST API backed by a local SQLite file and implements the API as a Vite dev-server middleware plugin.\n\n## Starting and verifying the server\n\n```bash\nPORT=8080 ./run.sh\n```\n\n`run.sh` installs dependencies if needed and then launches Vite in the foreground, bound to `127.0.0.1` on the port given by the `PORT` environment variable. Quick health checks:\n\n```bash\ncurl http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/health\n# → {\"ok\":true}\n\ncurl http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/v1/storage/status\n# → {\"driver\":\"sqlite\",\"schema_version\":1,\"initialized\":true}\n```\n\nStop the server with `Ctrl-C` in the terminal where it is running.\n\n## Entry point and major modules\n\n| File / directory | Responsibility |\n| ---------------- | -------------- |\n| `./run.sh` | Shell entry point. The middleware calls `route(req, res, next)`.\n3. `router.ts` parses the URL, checks the HTTP method, and dispatches to a handler.\n4. If a handler matches, it writes a JSON response and returns `true`; otherwise the router falls through to `next()` so Vite can serve static assets or the client entry point.\n5. Unhandled exceptions in the middleware are caught and returned as `500 {\"error\":\"internal server error\"}` if headers have not been sent yet.\n\n### POST body parsing\n\nPOST requests are read once from the stream and parsed as JSON. Malformed JSON returns `400 {\"error\":\"invalid json\"}` before any handler runs. Empty bodies are treated as `undefined`.\n\n## Main API / domain groupings\n\n| Group | Endpoints | Notes |\n| ----- | --------- | ----- |\n| Health | `GET /health` | Liveness probe. |\n| Storage | `GET /v1/storage/status`, `POST /v1/storage/reset` | Reports SQLite status and can reset the schema. |\n| Auth | `POST /v1/auth/register`, `POST /v1/auth/login` | Username/password registration; deterministic `session-<username>` token on login. |\n| Campaigns | `POST /v1/campaigns`, `GET /v1/campaigns/:id/state`, `POST /v1/campaigns/:id/characters`, `POST /v1/campaigns/:id/events` | Campaigns, characters, and event logs. |\n| Compendium | `POST /v1/compendium/monsters`, `GET /v1/compendium/monsters/:slug`, `POST /v1/compendium/items`, `GET /v1/compendium/items/:slug` | Bestiary and item references. |\n| Combat | `POST /v1/combat/sessions`, `POST /v1/combat/sessions/:id/conditions`, `POST /v1/combat/sessions/:id/advance` | Initiative order, conditions, and turn advancement. Do not introduce in-memory caches or module-level mutable state that affects responses.\n- **Preserve route precedence.** If you add a new endpoint, insert it in `src/lib/router.ts` in the correct historical order and return early when matched to avoid shadowing existing routes.\n- **Use existing validators.** Add new type guards to `src/lib/validation.ts` and reuse them in handlers.\n- **Keep rules pure.** Numerical calculations belong in `src/lib/rules.ts` so they can be unit-tested without a database or HTTP server.\n- **NodeNext imports.** Because `tsconfig.json` uses `\"moduleResolution\": \"NodeNext\"`, all relative imports must include the `.js` extension (e.g., `import { x } from './rules.js'`).
